research_scope: foundational primary research, scale validation, proposed diagnostic interview research, comorbidity studies, randomized self-guided intervention trial, current nosology limits, Arabic symptom-first search intent
nosology_note: Maladaptive daydreaming is an active research construct and is not currently established as an independent DSM-5-TR or ICD-11 diagnosis. The page must not present proposed criteria or MDS-16 cutoffs as a formal diagnosis.

sources.title: Maladaptive Daydreaming: A Qualitative Inquiry
sources.use: foundational qualitative description and historical origin of the research construct

sources.title: Maladaptive daydreaming: Evidence for an under-researched mental health disorder
sources.use: phenomenology, impairment, associated symptoms and comparison with non-maladaptive daydreaming

sources.title: Development and validation of the Maladaptive Daydreaming Scale (MDS)
sources.use: measurement development; supports research screening/measurement, not self-diagnosis

sources.title: Maladaptive daydreaming: Proposed diagnostic criteria and their assessment with a structured clinical interview
sources.publisher: Psychology of Consciousness: Theory, Research, and Practice
sources.use: proposed research criteria and structured interview; explicitly not an official DSM/ICD standard

sources.title: The Comorbidity of Daydreaming Disorder (Maladaptive Daydreaming)
sources.publisher: The Journal of Nervous and Mental Disease
sources.use: high rates of comorbid symptoms/diagnoses in a selected clinical research sample; not population prevalence

sources.title: Mindfulness meditation and self-monitoring reduced maladaptive daydreaming symptoms: A randomized controlled trial of a self-guided web-based program
sources.publisher: Journal of Consulting and Clinical Psychology
sources.use: first randomized evidence for a self-guided web-based intervention; promising but not sufficient to establish a universal treatment protocol

sources.title: Empowering the voice of individuals with maladaptive daydreaming: Research synthesis and clinical implications
sources.use: secondary context only; treatment and diagnostic claims remain anchored to the primary studies above

existing_site_overlap.decision: cross-link because immersive fantasy may coexist with dissociative symptoms, while maladaptive daydreaming is not simply equivalent to depersonalization/derealization
cross-link when repetitive or compulsive qualities are prominent; do not classify all immersive daydreaming as OCD
cross-link to distinguish verbal repetitive negative thinking from immersive narrative fantasy
cross-link when low mood, withdrawal or loss of functioning coexist; daydreaming itself does not diagnose depression
